title: Four Indian Americans Named to Thinkers50 Radar 2026
excerpt: Karunakaran, Sah, Tewari, and Dhar earn spots among the world's 30 most watched emerging management thinkers.
body:
Four Indian American leaders have secured spots on the Thinkers50 Radar Class of 2026 — the global list that identifies the 30 most promising management thinkers shaping the future of organisations and leadership. Thinkers50 announced the 10th annual Radar List on January 26, 2026, in partnership with the London Speaker Bureau, and the Indian American presence on it is impossible to miss.

**Who made the list and why:**
Arvind Karunakaran, an assistant professor at Stanford University's department of management science and engineering with a PhD from MIT Sloan, earns his place for research examining how AI tools affect skill development and worker well-being. Sunita Sah, a tenured professor at Cornell's Johnson Graduate School of Management, is recognised for her 2025 book *Defy*, which unpacks 'insinuation anxiety' — the psychological trap that nudges professionals into complying with bad advice rather than appear distrustful. Nidhi Tewari, a licensed clinical social worker, brings her 'science of attunement' to boardrooms, urging leaders to treat employees as whole human beings in her book *Working Well*. Vilas Dhar, President of the Patrick J. McGovern Foundation, is advancing what he calls a 'civic layer' for AI governance, a moral framework he traces to childhood summers in a rural Indian village.

**Why this list carries weight:**
Founded in 2001, Thinkers50 has grown into the premier global ranking of management thinkers. Its annual Radar list serves as an early-alert system for managers, publishers, and speaker bureaus worldwide. The Financial Times has called the Thinkers50 London Summit the 'Oscars of management thinking,' making a Radar mention a meaningful credential in global thought leadership.

**What to watch next:**
All four honorees are building bodies of work — on AI ethics, workplace psychology, and organisational governance — that could well earn them spots on Thinkers50's main ranking in the years ahead.
